title: Gap Filling & Cloze Tests
description: Master gap filling and cloze tests for Grade 9: choosing articles, prepositions, verbs, determiners and connectors from context — board-style passages with bilingual notes and tests.

topics.title: Grammar-Based Gap Filling
topics.concept:
Most gaps test a specific grammar point. Identify which one, then apply the rule:

  • Articles: a/an by sound; 'the' for something specific or unique.
  • Prepositions: rely on collocations — good at, afraid of, married to, depend on.
  • Verbs: match the tense to signal words and the verb to its subject.
  • Determiners: much/many, some/any, few/little by countability and sentence type.
  • Modals: choose by meaning — ability, obligation, possibility, advice.

Look at the words on both sides of the blank; they almost always reveal the answer.

examples.problem: Fill: He has been waiting ___ an hour.

recap: Identify the grammar point each gap tests
Articles by sound; prepositions by collocation; verbs by tense + agreement
Read the words on both sides of the blank for clues

topics.title: Cloze Tests — Strategy
topics.concept:
A cloze passage has several blanks; the answers connect into one coherent text. Strategy:

  1. Read the whole passage first to grasp the topic and tone.
  2. For each gap, decide the kind of word needed (article, verb, connector…).
  3. Use grammatical consistency — keep the tense and agreement steady across the passage.
  4. Use collocation and context — pick the word that partners naturally with its neighbours.
  5. Eliminate options that don't fit grammatically, then those that don't fit the meaning.
  6. Re-read with your answers to check the flow.

In multiple-choice cloze, the wrong options are often grammatically possible but make poor sense — so always test meaning, not just grammar.

examples.problem: Cloze: Trees give us shade. ___ , they clean the air. (connector)
examples.solution: Moreover / Also / Besides — a connector of addition fits the second benefit.
however / nevertheless — a contrast connector fits the surprising result.

recap: Read the entire passage before filling any gap
Keep tense and agreement consistent throughout
Use collocation, context and elimination; re-read to check flow

questions.q: Connector: 'It rained; ___ , the match was cancelled.'
Connector: 'He is rich; ___ , he is unhappy.'
Choose the word that best fits: 'The scheme aims ___ reducing pollution in cities.'
Fill the gap for correct flow: 'She had little money; ___ , she managed to travel widely.'
questions.explanation: A contrast between little money and wide travel → 'nevertheless'.

questions.q: Choose: 'No sooner ___ the announcement made than the crowd cheered.'
questions.explanation: Passive: 'No sooner was the announcement made than …'.

questions.q: Pick the correct verb form: 'By the time we arrive, the show ___ already started.'
Choose the determiner: 'There is ___ point in arguing now.'
Best connector: 'The bridge is old; ___ , it is still safe to use.'
Fill: 'He is not so much a writer ___ a journalist.'
questions.explanation: 'not so much … as …' is the fixed structure.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: 'She plays ___ violin beautifully.'

outcomes: Fill grammatical gaps with the correct word
Choose articles, prepositions and determiners from context
Supply the correct verb form (tense and agreement)
Read a whole passage before filling cloze gaps

intro.en: A gap-filling exercise removes a word and asks you to supply it; a cloze test does the same across a whole passage, so each answer must fit the flow, not just one sentence. The skill is to read first, then use grammar clues and word partnerships (collocations) to choose the one word that fits perfectly.
intro.hi: gap-filling में एक शब्द हटाकर पूछा जाता है; cloze test पूरे अनुच्छेद में यही करता है, इसलिए हर उत्तर को केवल एक वाक्य नहीं, बल्कि प्रवाह में फिट होना चाहिए। कौशल है — पहले पढ़ें, फिर व्याकरण-संकेतों और शब्द-संगति (collocations) से वह एक शब्द चुनें जो पूरी तरह सटीक बैठे।

real_life.situation:
You fill a form's sentence:

Gap: I have lived in Pune ___ 2015 and work ___ a software company.

Fill: …since 2015 and work for/at a software company.
real_life.why: 'since' fits a point in time, and 'for/at' fits the workplace. Each blank has a grammatical clue around it — that's exactly how gap-filling and cloze questions are solved.

fill_l2.instructions: Fill in the correct word (article, verb, determiner or connector).

items.q: She is ______ honest and hardworking girl.
He was tired; ______ , he kept working.
Each of the students ______ (have) a desk.

error_detection.sentence: He is the most tallest boy.
I have been ill since three days.
error_detection.correct: I have been ill for three days.

error_detection.sentence: It is a useful and a honest tool.
error_detection.correct: It is a useful and an honest tool.

sentence_correction.wrong: He succeeded although he was lazy.
sentence_correction.correct: He failed because he was lazy. (logic-based fill: use the connector that fits the meaning)

sentence_correction.wrong: She is married with a doctor.
sentence_correction.correct: She is married to a doctor.

sentence_correction.wrong: Much people came to the fair.
sentence_correction.correct: Many people came to the fair.

reading.passage:
Read this cloze passage; the suggested answers are in brackets.

Reading is one of (1)___ [the] best habits a student can develop. It improves (2)___ [our] vocabulary and (3)___ [helps] us think clearly. (4)___ [However], many young people now spend hours (5)___ [on] their phones instead. They should set (6)___ [aside] some time each day (7)___ [for] books, (8)___ [because] a single good book can change the way we see the world.

questions.q: What kind of word fills gap (1), and why 'the'?
questions.answer: An article; 'the best' is a superlative, which takes 'the'.
It is a contrast connector linking the benefit of reading with the opposite habit (phones).
(5) 'on their phones' and (7) 'time for books' are preposition gaps.

speaking: She is good at solving puzzles.
I have known him since childhood.
He was tired; however, he finished the race.
There isn't any milk in the fridge.
It is an honest and useful suggestion.

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph (4–5 sentences) and then blank out five words (one article, one preposition, one verb, one determiner, one connector) to make your own cloze test, with an answer key.
writing.example: I have lived here ___ (for) ten years. The neighbourhood is ___ (a) friendly place.

challenge.q: Choose the best connector: 'The plan was risky; ___ , we decided to try it.'
Fill the gap that fits the whole sentence: 'Hardly ___ he entered when the lights went out.'
challenge.explanation: 'Hardly had he entered when …' — inversion with 'had'.

challenge.q: Which word best completes both grammar and meaning? 'She spoke ___ confidence that everyone believed her.'
challenge.explanation: 'with such + noun + that' shows result: 'with such confidence that …'.
